sm: Ben Shapiro reacts to the news that Jensen Huang, the head of Nvidia, is out. He says he did not expect it, because Nvidia is an extraordinarily top-down company that Huang built over three decades, with something like 60 direct reports, so he ran it on his own institutional knowledge. Nvidia's CFO is reported to be serving as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent replacement, probably from outside. Ben mentions talk of bringing Tim Cook out of retirement, since Cook once followed an iconic founder at Apple. He notes that Nvidia controls an estimated 90 percent of the market for advanced AI chips. He warns that a CFO caretaker may cut research spending to protect margins, while Nvidia has always built its next chip months ahead, and a company can fall behind that way. He then turns to why Huang was ousted. Reports say Huang slept with a Chinese businesswoman, called Alice Huang, who was allegedly recruited by China's main spy agency, and that he told everyone in the company by letter. Another report mentions an affair with a staff member. Ben doubts that is the real reason, saying affairs are common among Silicon Valley leaders.

Ben argues the real reason is more likely a Wall Street Journal story that broke last night. It says Singapore was once about a fifth of Nvidia's revenue, then vanished from its financial disclosures almost overnight. Alice Huang ran a Singapore firm called Megaspede, likely a Chinese front company. The theory is that Nvidia shipped chips there and they were repackaged and sent on to China, which would be a major legal violation. The Journal reports Nvidia changed how it reports revenue by geography shortly after placing Megaspede on an internal block list. The board says it is investigating, and it describes Huang as the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Nvidia's stock fell about 14 percent in a day and then recovered a little, going from around 190 at the start of the week to around 165.

Ben adds that the Trump administration, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick in particular, may have known and done nothing, which raises questions about Lutnik's connections. He calls it a perfect storm for AI, combining sex, corruption and spying scandals at the biggest AI company. Democrats now have ammunition against the industry, claiming it cares only about China and worked with a corrupt administration. A counterargument is that China is honey-trapping AI leaders because it wants to win the AI race, so a crackdown on China would help the industry. Ben thinks Democrats are more likely to go after Nvidia's business broadly, and says Huang may be acting as a heat shield. He expects more details soon and says he will cover it more on tomorrow's show.
